text:
Carlos V: Hey all, new hire question — after switching to Colima my postgres container immediately fails with "could not create lock file "/var/lib/postgresql/data/postmaster.pid": Permission denied". I was using a host bind mount to ~/projects/app/pgdata. Also sporadically my app complains ERR NOAUTH when talking to Redis even though I set REDIS_PASSWORD in .env.local. Any quick ideas?

Meera S: welcome Carlos! two separate things commonly: 1) host bind mounts on Colima show up owned by root inside the VM; 2) multiple redis instances or env-file mismatches cause NOAUTH.

Meera S: For postgres we prefer a named volume in compose. If you need a host bind for seeded SQL, chown the dir inside Colima to the postgres uid (usually 999):
```bash
colima ssh
sudo chown -R 999:999 /home/you/projects/app/pgdata
exit
docker-compose up -d db
```

Jonah: If you used an alpine or slim postgres image it might not include extension packages (pgvector etc.). That will show up later as "could not open extension control file" during init. Use the repo dev image or build from Debian base and apt-install the extension.

Meera S: For the Redis NOAUTH: verify which env file docker-compose actually loads. If your compose file references `.env.dev` but you set variables in `.env.local` they won't be injected. Also compose CLI variants differ: `docker compose` (v2) supports `--env-file`.

Meera S: Quick checks:
```bash
# check which redis container is running
docker ps --filter ancestor=redis --format "table {{.Names}}\t{{.Image}}\t{{.Status}}"
# test redis auth inside container
docker-compose exec redis redis-cli -a "$REDIS_PASSWORD" ping  # should be PONG
# check env inside the running service
docker-compose exec redis env | grep REDIS
```

Carlos V: Running `docker ps` I indeed had an old `myproj_redis_1` leftover from another compose. Stopped it and `redis-cli -a` ping returns PONG now. For PG I did `colima ssh` and chowned the host dir to 999 and pg comes up. Thanks!

Jonah: Nice. If you still want host tools to hit the containerized db, consider mapping to a nonstandard host port to avoid collisions with a local postgres (brew). Eg `55432:5432` and point your host tools to localhost:55432.

Meera S: Also tip: if you switch from bind mounts to named volumes, remove the old (bad) mount before re-init: `docker-compose down -v` then `docker-compose up -d db` so the named volume gets initialised cleanly.

infra-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/local-db-setup  See sections: "Colima host mounts", "PG extensions in dev images", "Redis auth & env-file gotchas" :memo:

Carlos V: All fixed after removing the stale redis container and chowning the PG dir. One last Q: is it better to keep a host mount for SQL files or copy them into the image?

Jonah: For dev convenience we often COPY seed SQL into the image (or use an init-only named volume) so you don't need host mounts. If you actively edit SQL during development, a host mount is fine but expect permissions juggling on mac.

Carlos V: Perfect — thanks everyone. Happy to paste a short note of my steps to the runbook if helpful. Appreciate the warm welcome! :tada:
